text:
I'll describe this as carefully as I can, because for a long time I couldn't describe it at all.

I was 34, a primary school teacher, married, no children yet. My husband and I had been trying for a baby for two years without success and it was putting a lot of strain on us. A close friend of mine had done a psilocybin retreat in the Netherlands and came back glowing, saying it had helped her let go of years of grief. I booked the same retreat, partly hoping it would help me with the stress of trying to conceive, and partly, I think, because I wanted to feel something other than disappointment for a weekend.

The retreat was in a renovated farmhouse. There were ten participants and three facilitators, all very warm. On the first evening we sat in a circle and shared our intentions. I said I wanted to make peace with not being in control of my body. Everyone nodded. The facilitators talked about 'surrender' and 'trusting the medicine'.

The ceremony began the next morning. We drank truffle tea, lay down on mats with eyeshades, and the music began. The dose was high. I remember the come-up as a kind of heavy, sweet sinking, as if the floor were turning into honey. For about an hour it was beautiful. I saw fields of flowers, I felt my body as warm and alive, I cried softly about the babies I hadn't had.

Then the flowers turned into something else. They became wombs, hundreds of them, opening and closing, and every one was empty. I heard a sound like a heartbeat, but it was slowing, slowing, until it stopped. I understood, with absolute certainty, that I would never have a child. That my body was a barren place, that I had been born broken. The certainty was total. It wasn't a thought, it was a knowledge that went through every cell.

Then something worse happened. I started to see children, not my children, but children I knew: the children in my class. I saw their faces, one after another, and each one turned grey and still. I felt that I was being shown that I was a danger to children, that something in me was poisonous, that this was why my body wouldn't let me have one. I know how irrational this sounds now, but in that state it was the most real truth I'd ever encountered.

I tore off my eyeshade. The room was full of people lying on mats, and the facilitators moving quietly between them, and it looked like a field hospital, or a morgue. A facilitator came over and asked what was happening. I couldn't explain. I said 'I'm poison, I'm poison' over and over. She put her hand on my belly, I think meaning to comfort me, and I screamed, because that was exactly the place where the poison was.

I tried to get up and leave, but my legs wouldn't hold me, and I fell against the wall. Two facilitators guided me to a smaller side room with a mattress and stayed with me. One of them held my hand. I was sobbing so hard that I couldn't breathe properly, and I started to hyperventilate, and my hands cramped into claws. I thought I was dying. Part of me wanted to.

I went somewhere after that. I don't know how long it lasted. There was no room, no facilitators, no me. Just an endless grey plain with a cold wind, and the knowledge that I was alone and would always be alone, and that nothing would ever grow there. I wandered on that plain for what felt like years.

When I came back, it was afternoon. The facilitators were still there. One of them was crying too. They had been with me for five hours. They gave me water and a blanket and sat with me until the evening. In the closing circle I couldn't speak. My friend's glowing description of the retreat kept going through my head like a cruel joke.

I went home the next day. I told my husband it had been 'intense'. I didn't tell him the rest for months.

Ich habe auf einer Silvesterparty LSD genommen. Um Mitternacht ging das Feuerwerk los, und es war für mich wie ein Bombenangriff. Ich habe mich auf den Boden geworfen und die Hände über den Kopf gelegt. Jeder Knall war eine Explosion, jedes Licht ein Einschlag. Meine Freunde haben gelacht, weil sie dachten, ich mache Spaß, bis sie gesehen haben, dass ich weine. Ich habe mich in der Wohnung im Bad eingeschlossen und bin bis zum Morgen nicht herausgekommen.

Ich habe Pilze genommen und war allein in meiner Wohnung, als ich plötzlich das Gefühl hatte, dass sich mein Körper auflöst. Ich hatte panische Angst und wusste nicht, wie ich das stoppen kann. Ich habe mich ins Bett gelegt und mir die Decke über den Kopf gezogen und gewartet, bis es vorbei ist.

LSD at a lake. I watched a duck being taken by a pike, and it set off a horrible spiral about death and nature being cruel. I spent the rest of the trip crying about all the animals that die every second.

I had a very bad experience with ayahuasca that I didn't recognise as a bad experience until much later. I was at a retreat where the facilitators framed everything as healing: if you screamed, you were releasing trauma; if you shook, you were letting go of stuck energy; if you felt terror, the medicine was showing you your shadow. During my third ceremony I had the strongest experience of my life. I was being torn apart by animals, again and again, a jaguar, a pack of dogs, giant birds. Each time I felt the pain and the fear of dying. Between the attacks I was rebuilt, only to be torn apart again. It went on for hours. I screamed and begged. The facilitators sang louder and told me to surrender. Afterwards they said I had been through a 'shamanic dismemberment', which is apparently a well-known initiatory experience, and that I should feel honoured. I believed them, so I didn't ask for help when things went wrong afterwards.

Meine erste Erfahrung mit LSD war mit 18 auf einer Party. Ich war ziemlich naiv und habe eine ganze Pappe genommen, obwohl man mir gesagt hatte, eine halbe reicht. Ich hatte das Gefühl, mein Kopf explodiert, und dann war ich plötzlich nicht mehr da. Ich habe mich als Licht gefühlt, das sich überall verteilt. Als ich zurückkam, wusste ich nicht, wer ich bin, und habe meine Freunde gefragt, wie ich heiße. Sie haben mir das erst für einen Witz gehalten. Ich bin dann in Panik geraten und habe angefangen zu hyperventilieren. Ein Freund hat mich mit kaltem Wasser abgewaschen und mir immer wieder meinen Namen gesagt.

Mushrooms, about 3g, at home with my roommate. I got stuck in a loop where I kept 'waking up' from the trip, thinking it was over, and then realising I was still in it. Each time I woke up, things were slightly different, the furniture moved, my roommate's clothes changed colour. I counted maybe 40 loops. I became convinced I'd never wake up for real, that I'd be stuck in a nested dream forever. My roommate kept telling me where I was, but each time I thought he was part of the dream.

Took acid while visiting my grandmother in her care home, which was a stupid idea I'd had to 'see her soul'. The smells, the sounds of people moaning, my grandmother not recognising me, it all became a nightmare of decay and death. I fled to the car park and sat in the car for hours, crying.

Ich war in einer schweren Krise nach dem Tod meiner Frau und habe zum ersten Mal Psilocybin genommen, allein in unserem Haus. Ich hatte gehofft, sie zu spüren. Stattdessen habe ich die letzten Wochen ihres Lebens noch einmal erlebt, im Krankenhaus, ihr Gesicht, wie sie keine Luft mehr bekommt, das Piepen der Geräte. Ich war wieder dort, mit allen Gefühlen der Hilflosigkeit. Dann hat sich das Haus verwandelt. Jeder Gegenstand, ihre Brille, ihre Gartenhandschuhe, ihre Bücher, wurde zu einem Vorwurf. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass ich sie im Stich gelassen habe, dass ich mehr hätte tun müssen. Ich habe stundenlang auf ihrem Sessel gesessen, mich nicht bewegen können und mit ihr geredet, ohne dass sie geantwortet hat. Irgendwann habe ich gedacht, dass ich ihr folgen sollte. Ich habe meine Tochter angerufen, mitten in der Nacht, und sie ist sofort gekommen. Ohne sie weiß ich nicht, was passiert wäre.

I've used mushrooms a few times a year for a decade and never had a problem. One night I took my usual dose and something went wrong from the start. I felt a deep, physical sense of dread, like my body knew something terrible was coming. My heart was pounding, I was sweating and shaking. Nothing visual happened, no hallucinations, just pure terror that lasted for five hours. I lay on the floor of my living room with my eyes open, gripping the carpet, sure that I was about to die, though I had no idea of what. Afterwards I learned that I'd been coming down with a fever and that I'd also been under a lot of stress at work. I think my body was just in a bad state.

I'm an army medic. I'd seen a lot of injuries on deployment. Years later, I took mushrooms with my brother at a family cabin. At the peak, he cut his hand while chopping wood, quite a deep cut, a lot of blood. It wasn't life-threatening, but for me it was instantly the battlefield. I was back in a dusty compound with a soldier bleeding out under my hands, while I was actually wrapping my brother's hand in a kitchen towel. I did the right things, my hands knew what to do, but my mind was somewhere else entirely. I heard helicopters. I heard screaming. I saw my brother's face become the face of a young private I lost. When the bleeding was under control, I went outside and threw up and then lay down on the porch and shook for hours. My brother, with his bandaged hand, sat with me and kept saying 'I'm okay, I'm okay'. I couldn't believe him.

Ich habe mit Freunden in einer Kleingartenanlage Pilze genommen. Plötzlich stand ein Mann am Zaun und hat uns beschimpft und gedroht, die Polizei zu rufen. Für mich war er ein Dämon mit roten Augen. Ich bin weggerannt und habe mich in einem Gebüsch versteckt, bis es dunkel war.

I was at a large psytrance festival. On the third day, already sleep-deprived, I took a strong dose of LSD and then later someone gave me some 'extra' which I think was DMT or something similar. I lost all sense of the festival. I was in a different world, made of fractal geometry, endless and shifting, and I had no body. I felt that my consciousness was being stretched across infinity, thinner and thinner. Then the geometry started to break apart, like glass shattering, and behind it was black nothing. I felt myself being sucked in. I fought it with everything I had, but there was nothing to fight with.

When I came back, I was lying in a field far from the main stages, in the dark, alone. I had no idea how I'd got there. My phone and wallet were gone. I was wearing one shoe. I didn't know which day it was, or what country I was in. The music from the stages, far away, sounded like a huge machine grinding. I wandered for hours in the dark trying to find my tent. Every person I saw looked like a hollow shell. I asked a few people where I was, and they laughed. Someone gave me water. Eventually a festival volunteer found me and brought me to the welfare tent, where they kept me until morning and eventually found my friends through a lost-and-found board.

I'd lost about 14 hours that I can't account for.

Took mushrooms in a park with friends. A dog off its leash ran up and barked at me. I panicked and fell, and for the next hour was convinced the dog was a hellhound sent for me. Couldn't calm down even after it left.

Ich habe in einem Retreat Ayahuasca getrunken und eine sehr schwere Nacht erlebt. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass sich Schlangen um meinen Hals winden und mich erwürgen. Ich habe keine Luft mehr bekommen und gedacht, dass ich sterbe. Die Leiterin hat gesagt, das sei eine Reinigung meines Halschakras. Für mich war es einfach nur Todesangst, die Stunden gedauert hat.
